plot_data scales epoch/time axes and plots method curves with the repository color/linestyle map; this is the helper used by plot.py.

Author-linked polar branch configuration records FineWeb, GPT-2-Large dimensions, 1B-token training, learning-rate sweeps, weight decay and five-step settings; it is an experiment-setting source rather than a rendered-figure file.
Notebook markdown says it reproduces Figure 2; cell 4 calls plot_figure2(l1=0.03, n_steps=3, degree=5), and cell 1 specifies serif/Computer Modern, grid, line widths and export settings.
Package code supplies optimal_composition and the polynomial coefficients imported by plotsforpolar.ipynb; it supports the Figure 2 polynomial construction but is not itself a plotting file.

source_acquisition.search_note: The automated visual-source inventory row is no_public_source_found and the local corpus/visual_sources/iclr-2026-fe86008e62d4 directory plus visual_source_files_local.csv contain no acquired files. The PDF explicitly links the modichirag/GPT-opt polar branch; gh API verification found its author README, plot.py, gptopt/plot_utils.py, configuration and result JSON tree, but no exported figure assets and no matching plot source for Figures 3, 5, 7–10 or 14–18. The directly title-matched NoahAmsel/PolarExpress repository contains a notebook that explicitly reproduces Figure 2 and the underlying polar_express.py package. paper_style.palette_strategy: 正文 GPT-2 training family uses source-confirmed method colors: PolarExp #000000, You #8A2BE2, Jordan #FF0000 and AdamW #00518F, with line styles as partial redundancy. Theory Figure 2 uses three viridis-like polynomial colors; Figures 14–16 add Newton/SGD colors, Figure 17 uses method color × initializer line style, and Figure 18 uses dimension color × restart line style. Color carries most method identity in the dense multi-series plots, so gray-scale safety is mixed.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: The PDF has vector text, captions, axes, rules and chart paths for 17 figures; pdfimages identifies one 1592×471 RGB image with an alpha mask on p.5 (Figure 2). Thus the paper is mostly vector with one rasterized theory figure and vector surrounding text.
paper_style.style_consistency: Nimbus Roman No9 L/Computer Modern math, thin black axes, light dashed grids and a small serif plot grammar recur across main and appendix figures. The training family keeps PolarExp/You/Jordan semantics stable, while H.3 and J introduce additional local palettes. Figure 2 uses larger theory labels and the appendix dashboards compress labels but preserve the same serif frame.

figures.label: Figure 7

caption.text: Figure 7: Effects of stabilizing the update rules with a safety factor and cushioning, as described in Appendix G. The blue curve is the optimal degree-5 polynomial for the interval [0.005, 1]. It is has numerical issues because it maps singular values near 0.8 down to almost zero and maps 1 + ε to approximately u_{t+1} + 25ε. The stabilized version is better because it ensures p_t(x)/x ≥ 0.236 and maps all x ≤ 1.01 to at most u_{t+1}.

figures.label: Figure 9

caption.text: Figure 9: Impact of small singular directions of momentum matrix on optimization quality. We compare three variations of the Muon update rule. Exact Muon (green) processes the momentum M = UΣV^T by mapping each singular value to 1: polar(M) = UV^T. Truncated Muon (orange) maps the larger singular values to 1 and the smaller singular values to 0. Reverse Muon (blue) maps the larger ones to 1 and the smaller ones to −1. Computations are performed in bfloat32. All runs train GPT-2 Small on 1 billion tokens of FineWeb data with learning rate 0.05 and weight decay 0.1. When the cutoff that defines “large” and “small” singular values is γ ≈ 10^-3, all three methods perform well, showing that the small singular directions do not matter. Bottom panel shows the polynomial defined by composing five iterations of Polar Express. Five iterations is just enough for singular values ≥ 10^-3 to nearly converge.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 2 makes odd-polynomial interval contraction visible; Figure 3 connects the theorem metric to a real GPT-2 gradient; Figures 1/4/6 turn the approximation into Muon validation-loss comparisons; Figure 5 separates useful approximation accuracy from runtime. Appendix Figures 7–10 explain numerical stability and top-spectrum relevance, Figures 11–16 extend training/task slices and expose a cross-task boundary, and Figures 17–18 cover non-headline spectral-gap and rectangular-runtime extensions.
cross_object_system.caption_system: All captions begin with Figure N rather than a bold conclusion title. Main captions combine setup, panel key and best values; mechanism captions define line/interval semantics; H.2/H.3 captions define the panel grammar and three-seed bands. Figures 8/10 visibly contain light envelopes without a caption-level statistical definition, while Figure 15 retains a terminal comma from the PDF.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Not applicable: the 38-page PDF contains no Table object. Algorithm 1 (p.7), Algorithm 2 (p.25) and Algorithm 3 (p.36) are algorithm boxes, and the two Table references in the text point to cited works.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Theorem 3.1/3.3 and Figure 2 define the polynomial method; Figure 3 tests spectral convergence; Figures 1/4/6 compare Muon task outcomes; Figure 5 chooses 5–6 iterations and rejects exact SVD on cost grounds; Figures 7–10 isolate stabilization and effective singular directions; Figures 14–16 delimit cross-task transfer.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: The body calls Appendix A for code, C–E for proofs/equivalence, G for finite precision, H.1 for effective convergence and small singular directions, H.2 for training/time reruns, H.3 for image-classification failure cases, and I/J for extensions. The appendix figures preserve the main method colors where appropriate but add uncertainty bands only in H.3.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: PDF object fonts and rendered estimates give a stable Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern serif system, with plot labels around 6–10 pt and theory titles up to about 14 pt. The appendix 2×2 dashboards are denser, but panel titles, axis labels and captions follow the same hierarchy; source rcParams confirm serif/LaTeX and linewidth conventions for the training family.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: PolarExp black, You purple and Jordan red recur across the GPT-2 family; AdamW is deep blue when present. Green/orange/blue are reused locally for Newton/SGD, stabilization or dimensions, and line styles/markers provide some redundancy. Dense six-method H.3 curves remain color-dependent and are not fully gray-scale safe.

most_reusable_patterns: 用 Figure 2 的逐步函数—区间 storyboard 将理论 composition 变成可检查的状态转移。
用 Figure 3 的 synthetic + real-gradient 双 panel 连接 worst-case spectral metric 与实际对象，并明确 20-batch band。
用 Figure 5 的质量 bar + runtime bar 定义近似精度的 diminishing-return 决策面。
用 Figures 9/10 的 cutoff/有效子空间配对，把“任务足够精度”与“全谱精确”区分开。
用 Figures 14–16 保持同构并呈现跨任务 failure，限定 headline 的 transfer boundary。
highest_value_objects: Figure 2：公式—定理—Algorithm 1 的方法接口。
Figure 3：理论误差与真实 GPT-2 gradient 的机制证据。
Figure 5：Muon utility 与 exact-SVD runtime 的共同决策面。
Figures 9–10：small singular directions、top-spectrum 与 5–6 iteration 选择的桥。
Figures 14–16：对“consistent improvement”的跨任务边界与反例。
failure_patterns: 主 GPT-2 headline 多来自最佳学习率 sweep，缺少主实验 seed/不确定性。
训练图主要依赖颜色和小 legend；灰度、小尺寸及多方法比较的辨识度有限。
Figures 8/10 可见浅色包络却没有 caption-level 聚合/覆盖率定义。
Figure 7 的 “It is has” 语病与 Figure 15 的尾逗号属于 caption 质量问题。
Figures 17/18 的 synthetic/rectangular runtime 扩展没有直接连接到 Muon accuracy headline，需保持证据边界。
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: 论文用区间收缩理论图、谱误差机制图和 Muon loss/cost 消融构成主线，再用有效奇异子空间、训练复合图和跨任务失败图限定“5–6 步足够且优势可迁移”的边界。
